candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall handle and dispose of sewage sludge in accordance with Section 405 of the Clean Water Act and all other applicable Federal regulations to protect public health and the environment from any reasonably anticipated adverse effects due to any toxic pollutants which may be present.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether Section 405 and other applicable federal regulations impose enforceable numeric pollutant limits beyond those expressly listed in the permit determines which numeric limit applies when comparing reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: If requirements for sludge management practices or pollutant criteria become more stringent than the sludge pollutant limits or acceptable management practices in this permit, or control a pollutant not listed in this permit, this permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform to the requirements promulgated at Section 405(d)( 2) of the Clean Water Act.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether external pollutant criteria are more stringent than permit-listed limits, or control unlisted pollutants, could change which enforceable numeric limit governs a compliance comparison instead of the limits printed in the existing permit.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall give prior notice to EPA (Chief, Permits Branch, Water Management Division, Mail Code 6WQ -P, EPA Region 6, 1445 Ross Avenue, Dallas, Texas 75202) of any planned changes in the sewage sludge disposal practice, in accordance with 40 CFR Part 122.41(l)(1)(iii). These changes may justify the application of permit conditions that are different from or absent in the existing permit. Change in the sludge use or disposal practice may because for modification of the permit in accordance with 40 CFR Part 122.62(a)(1).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a disposal-practice change occurred and whether different or additional permit conditions were triggered affects which numeric limits, monitoring requirements, and missing-evidence expectations apply during Federal FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee or owner/operator shall submit a written closure and post closure plan to the permitting authority 180 days prior to the closure date.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether closure is planned or underway determines if this written submission obligation was applicable during the evaluated period and whether associated post-closure duties were in effect.

candidates.exact_span: A discussion of how the leachate collection system will be operated and maintained for three years after the surface disposal site closes if it has a liner and leachate collection system.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conditional phrase 'if it has a liner and leachate collection system' governs whether leachate-related operation, maintenance, and evidentiary expectations apply; different interpretations of site configuration change whether monitoring or documentation was required versus conditionally not required.

candidates.exact_span: A description of the system used to monitor continuously for methane gas in the air in any structures within the surface disposal site. The methane gas concentration shall not exceed 25% of the lower explosive limit for methane gas for three years after the sewage sludge unit closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage establishes both continuous methane monitoring in structures and an enforceable numeric ceiling (25% of the lower explosive limit); interpretation of which structures qualify and whether the three-year post-closure period applies changes applicable limits and monitoring obligations.

candidates.exact_span: A description of the system used to monitor for methane gas in the air at the property line of the site shall be included. The methane gas concentration at the surface disposal site property line shall not exceed the lower explosive limit for methane gas for three years after the sewage sludge unit closes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Property-line methane monitoring carries a distinct numeric limit (the lower explosive limit) and location scope; whether this obligation applies and how property-line measurements are identified changes limit applicability and required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: for three years after the sewage sludge unit closes
candidates.computation_change_reason: The post-closure three-year window defines when methane and related post-closure duties are operative; different interpretations of closure date or whether closure occurred during Federal FY2025 change which monitoring was required and how missing or non-numeric results should be classified.
